answer: To keep one operator from minting many names, each new agent must tend a leased 2.0 m bed on terrace 6 of the civic garden for 42 days, then mill 40 g of indigo pigment from plants grown only in that bed. The applicant posts 22 coins and a weekly dated photo of the bed tag. Peers accept when the HPLC fingerprint of the pigment matches the soil tag within 3% and the terrace stamp is in every frame. Pigment bought from a shop, or one bed used for two names, burns the stake and bars that plot for a year.
